tier_reason: latest-results.md compares ngtcp2 and quiche side by side in one harness, and all twelve cited p50 numbers match their rows; pairwise-comparisons.tsv confirms the publishable wins with 95% CIs (upload syscall 2.10x [2.06-2.11]). The harness code is public (perf.ngtcp2.h, perf.quiche.h, depofiles/) and flags are stated, but no CPU model is recorded, so it is not A; quicperf is a small personal harness (victorstewart/quicperf, 27 stars), not a well-known independent suite, so it is not B either (same rule applied earlier to chronoxor/CppSerialization, bemayer/xml-benchmark and prng-test-bench).

corrections.claimed_speedup: ~1.5-2.1x quiche on bulk-transfer scenarios (p50, syscall backend, derived from page data): download 18.227 vs 11.258 Gbps (1.62x), upload 31.047 vs 14.794 Gbps (2.10x), bidirectional 20.503 vs 12.662 Gbps (1.62x), multistream download 16.459 vs 10.990 Gbps (1.50x), multistream upload 24.816 vs 15.291 Gbps (1.62x), loss-recovery 17.379 vs 11.689 Gbps (1.49x), flow-control 15.600 vs 10.309 Gbps (1.51x); io_uring backend 1.35-1.71x. In the same run ngtcp2 is slower than quiche on request/response (0.80x), stream churn (0.70x), small-payload messages (0.71x), 0-RTT request/response (0.70x), close/reset cleanup (0.70x), connect (0.41x), resumed connect (0.37x) and DATAGRAM rate (0.29x), all syscall.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: quicperf C++ harness: CMake Release, -O3, native CPU flags, LTO by default (per README). ngtcp2 1.22.1 built from the release tarball via depofiles/ngtcp2.DepoFile (CMake, static, BoringSSL main-beddb58 backend); that depofile sets no extra optimisation flags of its own. quiche 0.29.0 (cloudflare/quiche commit e85fc8e) built via depofiles/quiche.DepoFile with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native -C opt-level=3", CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=fat, CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=1, --features ffi.
corrections.caveats: quicperf (victorstewart/quicperf, 27 stars) is an independent but small personal harness. Its committed run-environment file (docs/results/fixed-full-matrix-max16-20260601T175816Z/fixed-environment.txt) and adaptive-samples.tsv record only an anonymized machine_hash, with no CPU model, so hardware is not stated. That rules out Tier A, and the harness is not well known enough for B. The benchmark is loopback-only, with no physical or WAN link. The 2026-06-01 run was taken from a dirty working tree: the environment file's git status shows uncommitted edits to perf.ngtcp2.h, perf.quiche.h, perf.cpp and other adapters on top of commit 3eda036, so the committed code may not reproduce it exactly. The syscall download row (both libraries) and quiche's syscall bidirectional row are flagged 'inconclusive'. The publishable-only pairwise-comparisons.tsv still shows ngtcp2 winning upload, multistream, loss-recovery and flow-control rows at 1.35-2.10x. The win is limited to bulk transfer: ngtcp2 loses to quiche on every connection-setup and small-request scenario in the same run.

notes: Downgraded from B to C for the obscure-harness and no-CPU rule, and the low end of the claimed range corrected (loss recovery 1.49x and flow control 1.51x are below 1.6x). Metadata checks out: MIT, 1521 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-09-26, active. The record's tradeoffs field already notes the connect and request-rate losses.

tier_reason: latest-results.md compares TQUIC and quiche side by side in one harness, and all eight cited p50 numbers match their rows; pairwise-comparisons.tsv confirms each ratio with tight 95% CIs (for example reqresp syscall quiche/TQUIC 0.416 [0.406-0.421]). The code is public (perf.tquic.h, perf.quiche.h, depofiles/) and flags are stated, but no CPU model is recorded, so it is not A. quicperf is a small personal harness (27 stars), not a well-known independent suite, so it is not B. TQUIC's own tquic.net benchmark is first-party, gives charts only and states no compiler flags, so it is also C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: ~2.4x quiche on request/message-rate scenarios (p50, syscall backend, derived from page data): request/response 155,043 vs 64,574 rps (2.40x), stream churn 178,272 vs 74,756 streams/s (2.38x), small-payload messages 176,604 vs 73,852 msgs/s (2.39x), 0-RTT request/response 154,448 vs 65,327 rps (2.36x), close/reset cleanup 178,364 vs 75,080 streams/s (2.38x); io_uring backend 3.0-3.4x. In the same run TQUIC is slower than quiche on every bulk-throughput row (download 8.600 vs 11.258 Gbps; 0.76-0.96x across download, upload, bidirectional, multistream, loss-recovery and flow-control, syscall), on resumed connect (216 vs 301 conn/s, 0.72x) and on DATAGRAM rate (0.17x).
corrections.workload: quicperf: same shared C++ harness as the ngtcp2 entry, loopback UDP, CUBIC, shared TLS 1.3 Ed25519 material, one pinned server thread. The rows measure fresh-stream request/response rate, stream churn (open/send/receive/finish), tiny-message rate, 0-RTT request/response and close/reset cleanup, all with 16 client threads. A saturation scout chose the thread count; the published p50s come from 20 fixed randomized-block samples per row, with scout samples excluded.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: TQUIC pinned to commit 50f5a55 (2025-09-11, head of Tencent/tquic branch feature/support_datagram_extension_t2, not a tagged release) and built via depofiles/tquic.DepoFile: RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native -C opt-level=3", CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=fat, CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=1, --no-default-features --features ffi, linked against quicperf's BoringSSL (main-beddb58, via BORINGSSL_LIB_DIR). quiche 0.29.0 (commit e85fc8e) was built with the same RUSTFLAGS and LTO settings. The C++ harness uses CMake Release, -O3, native CPU flags and LTO by default.
corrections.caveats: quicperf (victorstewart/quicperf, 27 stars) is an independent but small personal harness. Its committed environment file (docs/results/fixed-full-matrix-max16-20260601T175816Z/fixed-environment.txt) and adaptive-samples.tsv record only an anonymized machine_hash, with no CPU model, so it is Tier C, not A or B. The benchmark is loopback-only. The 2026-06-01 run came from a dirty working tree (uncommitted edits to perf.tquic.h, perf.quiche.h and other adapters on top of commit 3eda036). TQUIC was measured at a feature-branch commit, not a release. The win is limited to request, stream and message rate: TQUIC loses to quiche on every bulk-throughput scenario in the same run. TQUIC's own first-party benchmark (https://tquic.net/docs/further_readings/benchmark; AMD EPYC 7K62, Linux 4.14, 'release mode', single-threaded servers, HTTP/3) does include Cloudflare quiche (QUICHE-CF v0.18.0), alongside QUICHE-G v118, NGINX-QUIC 1.25.2 and LSQUIC 4.0.1. It claims 'four to five times faster' than QUICHE-G and 'up to 20%' faster than LSQUIC, but gives charts only (no raw numbers, no compiler flags). Read approximately from the charts, TQUIC is about 1.2-1.5x QUICHE-CF on long connections and about 9x on 1 KB short connections. That page is first-party Tier C and is not the primary evidence here.

notes: Downgraded from B to C for the obscure-harness and no-CPU rule, and the claimed range corrected: all four cited ratios are 2.36-2.40x, not 2.1-2.4x. The original caveat was wrong that TQUIC's own benchmark omits Cloudflare quiche (QUICHE-CF v0.18.0 is in it). GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION, but LICENSE says TQUIC is Apache-2.0, with derived quiche (BSD-2), Chromium (BSD-3) and quinn (MIT) code, so Apache-2.0/copyable stands. Other metadata checks out: 1438 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2025-12-23, active. The record's tradeoffs field (not correctable here) quotes resumed connect as 216 vs 306 'syscall'; 306 is quiche's io_uring row, and its syscall row is 301.
